queries: Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet arxiv

sources_considered.why: ICLR 2024 paper (Google DeepMind authors) on LLMs' trouble correcting their own reasoning. It bears on the 'fact-check their own work' premise.
GPT-4 Technical Report showing strong exam and benchmark performance. This is context that cuts against a 'severely limited' reading.
The essay Marcus endorses. It is opinion and is not independent evidence about capacities.

receipt.public_excerpt: LLMs struggle to self-correct their responses without external feedback, and at times, their performance even degrades after self-correction.

evidence_items.explanation: Backs the narrower premise that LLMs had trouble checking and correcting their own reasoning around the post date. It does not establish the broad judgment of 'severely limited cognitive capacities'.

receipt.public_excerpt: While less capable than humans in many real-world scenarios, GPT-4 exhibits human-level performance on various professional and academic benchmarks, including passing a simulated bar exam with a score around the top 10% of test takers.

evidence_items.explanation: Shows the mixed picture. The developer reports both limits ('less capable than humans in many real-world scenarios') and strong benchmark results. Whether this adds up to 'severely limited' is a matter of judgment.

unresolved_gaps: There is no agreed metric or threshold for 'severely limited cognitive capacities', so the judgment cannot be scored against evidence.
